Nizami theorizes that Sultan Muhammad Ghori never appointed Aibak as his successor in India: the slave-general acquired this position after the Sultan's death through the use of diplomacy and military power. The Sultan's unexpected death left three of his main slave-generals – Aibak, Taj al-Din Yildiz, and Nasir ad-Din Qabacha – in positions of power.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The citizens of _____ requested him to assume sovereign power after the Sultan's death, and he moved his government to Lahore
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The citizens of Lahore requested him to assume sovereign power after the Sultan's death, and he moved his government to Lahore.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He informally ascended the throne on 25 June _____, but his formal recognition as a sovereign ruler happened much later, in 1208–1209
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He informally ascended the throne on 25 June 1206, but his formal recognition as a sovereign ruler happened much later, in 1208–1209.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Meanwhile, in and around _____, the Sultan's slaves fought with his nobles for control of the Ghurid Empire and helped his nephew Ghiyasuddin Mahmud ascend the throne
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, in and around Ghazni, the Sultan's slaves fought with his nobles for control of the Ghurid Empire and helped his nephew Ghiyasuddin Mahmud ascend the throne.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: When Mahmud had consolidated his rule, Aibak and other slaves sent messengers to his court, seeking deeds of manumission and investiture for ruling over the various _____ territories
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, in and around Ghazni, the Sultan's slaves fought with his nobles for control of the Ghurid Empire and helped his nephew Ghiyasuddin Mahmud ascend the throne. When Mahmud had consolidated his rule, Aibak and other slaves sent messengers to his court, seeking deeds of manumission and investiture for ruling over the various Ghurid territories.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Yildiz, who was Aibak's father-in-law, sought to control the _____ territories in India
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Meanwhile, in and around Ghazni, the Sultan's slaves fought with his nobles for control of the Ghurid Empire and helped his nephew Ghiyasuddin Mahmud ascend the throne. When Mahmud had consolidated his rule, Aibak and other slaves sent messengers to his court, seeking deeds of manumission and investiture for ruling over the various Ghurid territories.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, Aibak (unlike Yildiz) maintained the khutba and struck coins in Mahmud's name
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj, Aibak (unlike Yildiz) maintained the khutba and struck coins in Mahmud's name.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After Sultan Mahmud confirmed him as the ruler of _____ and manumitted him, Yildiz marched to Punjab, intending to take control of the region
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After Sultan Mahmud confirmed him as the ruler of Ghazni and manumitted him, Yildiz marched to Punjab, intending to take control of the region. Aibak marched against him, forced him to retreat to Kohistan, and took control of Ghazni.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak marched against him, forced him to retreat to _____, and took control of Ghazni
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak marched against him, forced him to retreat to Kohistan, and took control of Ghazni.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak then sent his representative _____ to Mahmud's headquarters at Firuz Kuh, seeking to expedite his request for the investiture
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak then sent his representative Nizamuddin Muhammad to Mahmud's headquarters at Firuz Kuh, seeking to expedite his request for the investiture.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____–1209, Mahmud conferred a chatr (ceremonial parasol) on Aibak, and issued a deed of investiture recognizing him as the ruler of Hindustan
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1208–1209, Mahmud conferred a chatr (ceremonial parasol) on Aibak, and issued a deed of investiture recognizing him as the ruler of Hindustan.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to Minhaj's _____-i Nasiri, Mahmud styled Aibak as a "Sultan"; chronicler Hasan Nizami also calls him a "Sultan"
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj's Tabaqat-i Nasiri, Mahmud styled Aibak as a "Sultan"; chronicler Hasan Nizami also calls him a "Sultan".

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: No coins issued by him have been found, and no extant coins describe him as a "_____"
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj's Tabaqat-i Nasiri, Mahmud styled Aibak as a "Sultan"; chronicler Hasan Nizami also calls him a "Sultan". No coins issued by him have been found, and no extant coins describe him as a "Sultan".

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, Aibak became complacent and devoted his time to pleasures and amusements in Ghazni
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj's Tabaqat-i Nasiri, Mahmud styled Aibak as a "Sultan"; chronicler Hasan Nizami also calls him a "Sultan". According to Minhaj, Aibak became complacent and devoted his time to pleasures and amusements in Ghazni.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The people of _____ invited Yildiz to evict him from the city, and when Yildiz arrived in the vicinity of Ghazni, Aibak panicked and escaped to India via a narrow mountain pass called Sang-i Surkh
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj, Aibak became complacent and devoted his time to pleasures and amusements in Ghazni. The people of Ghazni invited Yildiz to evict him from the city, and when Yildiz arrived in the vicinity of Ghazni, Aibak panicked and escaped to India via a narrow mountain pass called Sang-i Surkh.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Ali Mardan Khalji, who had accompanied Aibak to _____, was captured and imprisoned by Yildiz
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj, Aibak became complacent and devoted his time to pleasures and amusements in Ghazni. The people of Ghazni invited Yildiz to evict him from the city, and when Yildiz arrived in the vicinity of Ghazni, Aibak panicked and escaped to India via a narrow mountain pass called Sang-i Surkh.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak dispatched him to _____ in Bengal, where Husamuddin Iwaz agreed to be his subordinate
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak dispatched him to Lakhnauti in Bengal, where Husamuddin Iwaz agreed to be his subordinate.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In _____, he fell down from a horse while playing chaugan (a form of polo on horseback) in Lahore, and died instantly when the pommel of the saddle pierced his ribs
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1210, he fell down from a horse while playing chaugan (a form of polo on horseback) in Lahore, and died instantly when the pommel of the saddle pierced his ribs.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, his generosity earned him the epithet lakh-bakhsh, literally "giver of lakhs [of copper coins or jitals]"
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj, his generosity earned him the epithet lakh-bakhsh, literally "giver of lakhs [of copper coins or jitals]".

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The 16th century _____ chronicler Abu'l-Fazl criticizes Mahmud of Ghazna for "shedding innocent blood", but praises Aibak stating that "he achieved things, good and great"
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The 16th century Mughal chronicler Abu'l-Fazl criticizes Mahmud of Ghazna for "shedding innocent blood", but praises Aibak stating that "he achieved things, good and great".

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: As late as the 17th century, the term "Aibak of the time" was used to describe generous people, as attested by the chronicler _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: As late as the 17th century, the term "Aibak of the time" was used to describe generous people, as attested by the chronicler Firishta.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, his Gujarat campaign resulted in the enslavement of 20,000 people; and his Kalinjar campaign resulted in the enslavement of 50,000 people
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Hasan Nizami, his Gujarat campaign resulted in the enslavement of 20,000 people; and his Kalinjar campaign resulted in the enslavement of 50,000 people.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, Nizami's work is full of rhetoric and hyperbole, so these numbers seem to be exaggerated, however, the number of slaves collected must indeed have been vast and grew over time
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Irfan Habib, Nizami's work is full of rhetoric and hyperbole, so these numbers seem to be exaggerated, however, the number of slaves collected must indeed have been vast and grew over time.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After his death, the _____ officers (maliks and umara) stationed at Lahore appointed Aram Shah as his successor
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After his death, the Turkic officers (maliks and umara) stationed at Lahore appointed Aram Shah as his successor. Some Turkic officers then invited Aibak's former slave Iltutmish, a distinguished general, to take over the kingdom.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: No details about _____'s life are available before his ascension to the throne
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After his death, the Turkic officers (maliks and umara) stationed at Lahore appointed Aram Shah as his successor. No details about Aram Shah's life are available before his ascension to the throne.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Some Turkic officers then invited Aibak's former slave _____, a distinguished general, to take over the kingdom
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Some Turkic officers then invited Aibak's former slave Iltutmish, a distinguished general, to take over the kingdom. Aibak had purchased Iltutmish sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in 1197.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak had purchased _____ sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in 1197
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Some Turkic officers then invited Aibak's former slave Iltutmish, a distinguished general, to take over the kingdom. Aibak had purchased Iltutmish sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in 1197.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aibak had purchased Iltutmish sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak had purchased Iltutmish sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in 1197.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: According to _____, Aibak looked upon Iltutmish as the next ruler: he used to call Iltutmish his son and had granted him the iqta' of Badaun
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: According to Minhaj, Aibak looked upon Iltutmish as the next ruler: he used to call Iltutmish his son and had granted him the iqta' of Badaun.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Consequently, the nobles appointed Iltutmish as _____'s successor and married Aibak's daughter to him
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Consequently, the nobles appointed Iltutmish as Aram Shah's successor and married Aibak's daughter to him. Aram Shah challenged Iltutmish's claim to the throne but was decisively defeated and killed after a military conflict.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Aram Shah challenged _____'s claim to the throne but was decisively defeated and killed after a military conflict
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Aibak had purchased Iltutmish sometime after the conquest of Anhilwara in 1197. According to Minhaj, Aibak looked upon Iltutmish as the next ruler: he used to call Iltutmish his son and had granted him the iqta' of Badaun.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Iltutmish subjugated the rebel governors and transformed the loosely-held Ghurid territories of India into the powerful _____
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Iltutmish subjugated the rebel governors and transformed the loosely-held Ghurid territories of India into the powerful Delhi Sultanate.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Iltutmish was succeeded by his family members, and then by his slave _____ ud din Balban
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Iltutmish was succeeded by his family members, and then by his slave Ghiyas ud din Balban.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: This line of kings is called _____ or Slave dynasty; however, this term is a misnomer
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: This line of kings is called Mamluk or Slave dynasty; however, this term is a misnomer.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Only Aibak, _____, and Balban were slaves, and seem to have been manumitted before their ascension to the throne
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Iltutmish subjugated the rebel governors and transformed the loosely-held Ghurid territories of India into the powerful Delhi Sultanate. Iltutmish was succeeded by his family members, and then by his slave Ghiyas ud din Balban.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Today his tomb is located in _____, Lahore
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Today his tomb is in Anarkali, Lahore.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The tomb was built, in its present form, during the 1970s by the _____ of Archaeology and Museums (Pakistan) which tried to emulate the Sultanate-era architecture
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The tomb was built, in its present form, during the 1970s by the Department of Archaeology and Museums (Pakistan) which tried to emulate the Sultanate-era architecture.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Before the modern construction, the _____'s grave existed in a simple form and was enclosed by residential houses
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The tomb was built, in its present form, during the 1970s by the Department of Archaeology and Museums (Pakistan) which tried to emulate the Sultanate-era architecture. Before the modern construction, the Sultan's grave existed in a simple form and was enclosed by residential houses.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Historians dispute whether a proper tomb ever existed over it (some historians claim that a marble dome did stand over it but was destroyed by the _____)
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Historians dispute whether a proper tomb ever existed over it (some historians claim that a marble dome did stand over it but was destroyed by the Sikhs).

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: However, this may have been an erroneous addition made by a careless scribe, as _____-i-Juwayni's Tarikh-i-Jahan-Gusha chronicle explicitly mentions that Aibak had no son
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: However, this may have been an erroneous addition made by a careless scribe, as Alauddin Ata Malik-i-Juwayni's Tarikh-i-Jahan-Gusha chronicle explicitly mentions that Aibak had no son.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Contrarily, the 14th century historian _____ stated Aaram Shah as Aibak's real son
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Contrarily, the 14th century historian Abdul Malik Isami stated Aaram Shah as Aibak's real son.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The first one was married to Nasir ad-_____, the Ghurid governor of Multan
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The first one was married to Nasir ad-Din Qabacha, the Ghurid governor of Multan.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: After her death, the second daughter was married to _____ as well
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The first one was married to Nasir ad-Din Qabacha, the Ghurid governor of Multan. After her death, the second daughter was married to Qabacha as well.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The third one was married to Aibak's slave Iltutmish, who succeeded _____ on the throne of Delhi
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The third one was married to Aibak's slave Iltutmish, who succeeded Aram Shah on the throne of Delhi.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He also mentions that the Hindu temples at Meerut and _____ were converted into mosques during Aibak's reign; these included "a thousand temples" in Delhi alone
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He also mentions that the Hindu temples at Meerut and Kalinjar were converted into mosques during Aibak's reign; these included "a thousand temples" in Delhi alone.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He further claims that Aibak freed the whole Kol (_____) region from idols and idolatry
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He further claims that Aibak freed the whole Kol (Aligarh) region from idols and idolatry.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: At some point, Aibak's army started recruiting _____ soldiers
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Nizami's claim that the remains of the demolished Hindu temples were used to build mosques is corroborated by architectural remains, such as those at the Qutb Minar complex in Delhi and the Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra in Ajmer. At some point, Aibak's army started recruiting Hindu soldiers.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: His army at the siege of Meerut (_____) is known to have included Hindu soldiers
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: His army at the siege of Meerut (1192) is known to have included Hindu soldiers.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Similarly, the "forces of Hindustan" (Hasham-i Hindustan) that accompanied him to Ghazni in _____, included Hindu chiefs ("ranas" and "thakurs")
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Similarly, the "forces of Hindustan" (Hasham-i Hindustan) that accompanied him to Ghazni in 1206, included Hindu chiefs ("ranas" and "thakurs").

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: The composition of _____'s Tajul-Ma'asir, which was completed during the reign of Iltutmish, probably began during Aibak's reign
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: The composition of Hasan Nizami's Tajul-Ma'asir, which was completed during the reign of Iltutmish, probably began during Aibak's reign.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Firishta (17th century), however, dates the rebellion to 1203, and states that Jatwan retreated to the frontiers of _____ after his defeat
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Firishta (17th century), however, dates the rebellion to 1203, and states that Jatwan retreated to the frontiers of Gujarat after his defeat. He was later killed as a subordinate of the Chaulukya king Bhima II when Aibak invaded Gujarat.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In 1192, he took control of _____ and Baran (modern Bulandshahr), from where he would later launch attacks against the Gahadavala kingdom
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1192, he took control of Meerut and Baran (modern Bulandshahr), from where he would later launch attacks against the Gahadavala kingdom.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: He also took control of Delhi in 1192, where he initially retained the local _____ ruler as a vassal
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He also took control of Delhi in 1192, where he initially retained the local Tomara ruler as a vassal. In 1193, he deposed the Tomara ruler for treason and took direct control of Delhi.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In 1193, he deposed the _____ ruler for treason and took direct control of Delhi
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He also took control of Delhi in 1192, where he initially retained the local Tomara ruler as a vassal. In 1193, he deposed the Tomara ruler for treason and took direct control of Delhi.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In 1197, Aibak defeated the _____ army at Mount Abu, thus avenging Muhammad Ghori's defeat at the Battle of Kasahrada nearly two decades earlier
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Supported by the Chaulukyas, who ruled Gujarat in the south, the Mhers posed a serious threat to Aibak's control of the region. In 1197, Aibak defeated the Chaulukya army at Mount Abu, thus avenging Muhammad Ghori's defeat at the Battle of Kasahrada nearly two decades earlier.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In 1204, _____ suffered a defeat against the Khwarazmians and their allies at the Battle of Andkhud, followed by several challenges to his authority
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1204, Muhammad Ghori suffered a defeat against the Khwarazmians and their allies at the Battle of Andkhud, followed by several challenges to his authority. Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: On 15 March 1206, _____ was assassinated: different sources variously attribute the act to Khokhars or Ismailis
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: In 1204, Muhammad Ghori suffered a defeat against the Khwarazmians and their allies at the Battle of Andkhud, followed by several challenges to his authority. On 15 March 1206, Muhammad Ghori was assassinated: different sources variously attribute the act to Khokhars or Ismailis.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Minhaj states that at the time of _____'s death in 1206, the Ghurids controlled the following areas in India: However, Ghurid control was not equally effective in all these areas
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Minhaj states that at the time of Sultan Muhammad Ghori's death in 1206, the Ghurids controlled the following areas in India: However, Ghurid control was not equally effective in all these areas. Bakhtiyar was killed by his subordinate Ali Mardan Khalji at Devkot in 1206, around the same time Sultan Muhammad Ghori was assassinated.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: Bakhtiyar was killed by his subordinate _____ at Devkot in 1206, around the same time Sultan Muhammad Ghori was assassinated
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: Bakhtiyar was killed by his subordinate Ali Mardan Khalji at Devkot in 1206, around the same time Sultan Muhammad Ghori was assassinated.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.question: In 1208–1209, _____ conferred a chatr (ceremonial parasol) on Aibak, and issued a deed of investiture recognizing him as the ruler of Hindustan
Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: After Sultan Mahmud confirmed him as the ruler of Ghazni and manumitted him, Yildiz marched to Punjab, intending to take control of the region. Aibak then sent his representative Nizamuddin Muhammad to Mahmud's headquarters at Firuz Kuh, seeking to expedite his request for the investiture.

Qutb ud-Din Aibak.fact: He came from Turkestan, and belonged to a Turkic tribe called Aibak. The word "Aibak", also transliterated as "Aibek" or "Aybeg" derives from the Turkic words for "moon" (ai) and "lord" (bek).
